source.note: Institution-level Key Stage 2 attainment from the DfE Explore Education Statistics API. Built for parental choice comparison, not school governance. Progress measures are sparse for 2024/25 because of missing KS1 baselines. On-demand local authority pack: City of London (seed maintained set remains Hampshire).  Secondary-age state and independent schools carry Key Stage 4 and 16–18 (A-level) outcomes where published (nil/zero English & maths GCSE returns cleared; EBacc subject pillars used as fallbacks when possible). Independents also carry Ofsted grades for non-association schools and GIAS inspectorate/website links for ISI schools (ISI search prefers postcode). Independents carry GIAS inspectorate/website links for ISI schools, with profile + latest DownloadReport citation when resolvable. Inspection précis fields are verbatim excerpts from the latest Ofsted or ISI report PDF, with footnote links to the source file.

independent.note: Mean of independents in this index with usable KS4 figures (nil/zero returns removed); KS5 means use A-level APS where published

stateKs4.note: Mean of state schools in this index with usable KS4 figures (nil/zero returns removed); KS5 means use A-level APS where published

phonics.note: DfE publishes phonics screening results for England and local authorities only — not for individual schools. KS1 teacher assessment is no longer collected nationally (from 2023/24).

schools.inspectionPrecis: The school provides a welcoming and purposeful community in which staff know pupils well as individuals and support them to develop independence, confidence and resilience. Leaders provide a clear ethos for learning and behaviour, which is reflected in pupils’ positive attitudes to learning and willingness to take responsibility within the school community.

inspectionQuotes.text: Leaders monitor pupils’ progress through regular review of assessment information.
Some teachers do not provide guidance and feedback to pupils to help them to improve their understanding and work.

inspectionStrengths.text: Pupils use their knowledge through creative, technological and enterprise activities that encourage them to explore ideas, develop curiosity and achieve well.

schools.name: City of London School
schools.inspectionPrecis: Governors maintain efficient oversight of the work of leaders, ensuring that they carry out their responsibilities effectively. Leaders’ strategic planning reflects a clear vision and thorough evaluation of the school’s successes and areas for improvement. Leaders carefully consider any potential risks to pupils’ wellbeing and put effective measures in place to mitigate these.

inspectionQuotes.text: Pupils make good progress across all subjects.
Leaders cultivate a culture in which listening to pupils is integral.

inspectionStrengths.text: Leaders carefully consider any potential risks to pupils’ wellbeing and put effective measures in place to mitigate these.
Mechanisms such as the ‘pupil parliament’ and the tutor system, as well as the open attitudes of staff, enable pupils to voice opinions and suggest improvements.
The curriculum is broad and designed to promote high academic standards and the school’s values of kindness, readiness, and awareness.

inspectionImprovements.text: Leaders should:  ensure that staff make certain that all pupils consistently follow the rules for movement in the corridors.

schools.name: David Game College
schools.inspectionPrecis: School leaders achieve an effective balance between offering an education which encompasses personal development along with a focus on pupils gaining the knowledge required for examination success. Leaders have appropriate skills and knowledge to promote pupils’ wellbeing and to enable pupils to make good academic progress.

inspectionQuotes.text: Staff encourage pupils to be focused and ambitious about their work.
Pupils are well motivated, and their positive behaviour is supportive of learning.

inspectionStrengths.text: Leaders have appropriate skills and knowledge to promote pupils’ wellbeing and to enable pupils to make good academic progress.
Consequently, different groups of pupils, including those with special educational needs or disabilities (SEND), make good progress.
Pupils have access to individualised learning and tutorial support, as well as teaching which is well planned, and which uses suitable methods and resources.

inspectionImprovements.text: Advice about pupils’ future pathways is largely effective, although it is inconsistent when it depends on the varying quality of individual tutorial support.

schools.name: St Paul's Cathedral School
schools.inspectionPrecis: Leaders and governors demonstrate a shared commitment to the school’s values, which are evident in the quality of relationships across the community and are reflected consistently in curricular provision. These values underpin a positive and purposeful ethos in which pupils feel supported and develop a substantial sense of belonging. Leaders’ thoughtful approach to strategic planning ensures that the school’s aims are translated effectively into practice, supported by coherent development planning at whole-school and departmental levels.

inspectionQuotes.text: Staff pay careful and sensitive attention to individual pupils’ needs.
Leaders have established a highly effective chorister programme, underpinned by a nurturing and well-organised boarding provision, which enables pupils to flourish both academically and musically.

inspectionStrengths.text: These values underpin a positive and purposeful ethos in which pupils feel supported and develop a substantial sense of belonging.
Leaders ensure that appropriate policies are made available to parents and that procedures are implemented effectively.

schools.inspectionPrecis: Pupils grow into active citizens at this school. They are proud and happy to come to school every day. From the very youngest child, they follow the school’s clear expectations of how to treat one another. As a result, pupils at this school are kind and caring to all members of the school community. Their behaviour is exceptional because they understand the high standards expected and the routines to follow. The school prides itself on providing many rich opportunities to its pupils. Every pupil learns to play the violin, cello or double bass by the time they leave the school. Many showcase their talent and skill through public performances. The provision for music is remarkable.
